texts.li: [lastwinter] The autumn count is done: {A_nameDef} walked every pen and made it {HEAD} head. The hay and kibble in store will feed them about {FEED} days, and last winter the cold held for {WINTER} days. {A_nameDef} asks the council what the colony keeps through to spring. {B_nameDef} would rather not part with a single one.

[!lastwinter] {A_nameDef} has counted the herd, {HEAD} head in all, and set it against the stores: hay and kibble for about {FEED} days, and a winter ahead of some {WINTER} days. What goes, and what stays? {B_nameDef} has already said what {B_pronoun} thinks of selling good stock.

[lowtech] Every autumn the old herders counted their beasts and counted their hay, and {A_nameDef} has done the same: {HEAD} head, and feed for about {FEED} days. The young ones could go to the next traders, or the oldest to the knife for the winter's meat. {B_nameDef} says the herd is the colony's wealth and should be kept whole.

[skill:Animals] {A_nameDef} knows every animal in the pens and has counted them twice: {HEAD} head. The yearlings would fetch a fair price from the next traders, and the oldest would see the colony through the cold in meat. {B_nameDef} would sooner stretch the hay and keep them all.

[short,lastwinter] {A_nameDef} came back from the pens with a long face: {HEAD} head, and hay for {FEED} days, when last winter the cold held for {WINTER} days. Something has to give before the snow, {A_pronoun} says. {B_nameDef} asks the council to remember that the herd took years to build.

li.label: Keep them all
li.outcome: The council keeps the whole herd through the winter. {A_nameDef} will stretch the hay and hope for an early spring.

li.label: Sell the yearlings to the next traders
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has picked out the yearlings to sell. When the next traders stop at the colony, {A_pronoun} will go down to the pens for them, and the trade window has them marked to sell.

li.label: {COUNT} of the oldest to the butcher
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has marked {COUNT} of the oldest for slaughter, never the herd's leader nor anyone's own. The stores will have meat for the winter, and the hay will go further.
